steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three high-impact strategies cities can adopt to cut their greenhouse-gas emissions:

1. Shift how people move  
   • Expand reliable, high-frequency public transit (bus rapid transit, light rail, metro) so residents can travel without private cars.  
   • Build safe infrastructure for walking and cycling—protected bike lanes, traffic-calmed streets, ample sidewalks—encouraging zero-emission trips.  
   • Introduce demand-management tools such as congestion pricing, limited parking supply and low-emission zones to discourage fossil-fuel car use while funding cleaner transport options.  

2. Upgrade buildings and urban energy systems  
   • Tighten energy-efficiency standards for new construction (passive-house or net-zero codes) and launch large-scale retrofits of existing buildings with better insulation, high-performance windows and smart controls.  
   • Replace fossil-fuel heating with electric heat pumps and district energy networks that use waste heat or renewables.  
   • Deploy rooftop solar, community solar gardens and battery storage so buildings both consume and generate clean electricity.  

3. Decarbonize municipal services and local industry  
   • Electrify city vehicle fleets—buses, garbage trucks, taxis—and supply them with renewable electricity; install widespread EV charging infrastructure for residents.  
   • Capture and utilize methane from wastewater treatment plants and landfills; convert organic waste to biogas or compost instead of letting it emit in open dumps.  
   • Adopt green procurement policies (e.g., low-carbon concrete, recycled steel) and support local circular-economy businesses that lower embodied emissions in materials and goods flowing through the city.
